Business Delegate.why: Named J2EE core pattern in Sun's catalogue, used in enterprise codebases.

Event Aggregator.why: Named enterprise pattern from Fowler's PoEAA. Specialist tier fits.

Adapter.why: GoF pattern. Widely known, so NPE tier is reasonable.

Dependency Injection.why: Named pattern (Fowler, Martin), but not among the first answers most people give. Off-by-one overstates it.

Saga.why: Named distributed-transaction pattern (Garcia-Molina and Salem, 1987). Systems and domain people know it, so Memory leak fits.

API Gateway.why: Named microservices pattern (Richardson, Microsoft). Systems and domain people know it.

Dirty Flag.why: Named game-programming pattern (Nystrom). Specialist tier fits.

Active Object.why: Named concurrency pattern (POSA2). It belongs with specialists (Race condition), not a memory-related tier.

Execute Around.why: Short form of Beck's named 'Execute Around Method' (Smalltalk Best Practice Patterns). Shortened name, but the sample lists it as its own kind. Tier is plausible.

Data Access Object.why: Named core J2EE pattern. DAO is a plain abbreviation, which is an alias. NPE tier is reasonable.

Composite View.why: Named J2EE core pattern. Specialist tier fits.

Collecting Parameter.why: Named Smalltalk pattern from Beck. Specialist tier fits.

Queue-Based Load Leveling.why: Named cloud design pattern (Microsoft Azure Architecture Center). Specialist tier fits.

Subclass Sandbox.why: Named Beck Smalltalk pattern, but obscure. Heisenbug fits better than Race condition.

Update Method.why: Named Beck Smalltalk pattern, but obscure. Heisenbug fits better than Race condition.

Fork-Join.why: Named parallel-computing pattern (Lea, Java ForkJoinPool). Parallel programmers know it, so Race condition fits. Memory leak does not.

Role Object.why: Named design pattern (Riehle et al., PLoPD). Deep-internals tier fits.

Null Object.why: Named pattern (Woolf, Martin, PLoPD3). Its null-related name suits the NPE tier.

Proxy.why: GoF pattern. 'dynamic proxy' is a Java API binding of the generic name, so it is an alias; 'Proxy pattern' and 'Proxy design pattern' are punctuation or inflection aliases. NPE tier is reasonable.

Parameter Object.why: Fowler's refactoring (Introduce Parameter Object). It is a named refactoring, not a GoF pattern or a pattern-language entry. I am not sure it falls under the Accepts line. The NPE tier also overstates how well known it is.
